title: Predictive Warmup and Cold-Start Economics PRD and Rollout Playbook
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Summary:
This PRD defines the Predictive Warmup and Cold-Start Economics initiative: a product + runtime feature set to reduce tail latency from cold model starts while minimizing incremental cost. It combines a telemetry-driven prediction engine, prioritized pre-warming policies, and economics-aware retention/eviction heuristics.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce 99th-percentile request latency caused by cold-starts for hosted inference by 40% within first 3 months after launch (baseline: 220ms cold-start tail).
- Keep incremental cost for warmup capacity under 7% of total hosted GPU spend for 80% of customers in experiment cohort.
- Maintain correctness and quality: <0.1% increase in error/misroute incidents attributable to warmup.

Background and motivation:
Many real-world workloads on Redwood experience occasional cold-start latency spikes when model containers (or GPU contexts) are evacuated, evicted, or not yet allocated. Current mitigations (fixed warm pools, overprovisioning) either waste budget or are brittle across multi-tenant workloads. Predictive Warmup aims to trade a small, measured cost increase for deterministic latency improvements, with automated rollback and conservative defaults for cost-sensitive tenants.

Key concepts and vocabulary:
- Cold-start: any request served by a model variant instance that requires non-trivial initialization (model weights loading, kernel JIT, kv-cache warm) exceeding baseline steady-state generation latency.
- Warmup instance: a provisioned model worker that has completed all initialization steps and is ready to accept requests with steady-state latency characteristics.
- Prediction window: the lookahead horizon (in seconds) used by the predictor to decide whether to pre-warm. Default: 60s.
- Warmth credit: a short-lived token tracked per-tenant representing budgeted warm instances; used for accounting in the cost model.

User stories and personas:
- ML Platform Engineer (enterprise): "I need 99th-percentile latency guarantees for my conversational application during daily traffic spikes, but I want to cap additional warmup spend to 5%."
- Product Developer (startup): "I can accept occasional warmup latency but want a simple on/off toggle and a safety cap so my dev credits aren’t depleted."
- SRE (Redwood): "Operators need visibility into warmup decisions, ability to quarantine predictive logic, and run experiments safely at host level."

High-level design:
1) Signal ingestion and prediction
- Inputs: per-tenant request rate, session churn, route-level SLO breaches, recent eviction history, regional capacity health, time-of-day signals, and synthetic heartbeat probes.
- Predictor: lightweight time-series classifier running in Optimize Conductor (service: optimize-predictor). Uses a gradient-boosted model for throughput-features and a bayesian prior to avoid overreaction.
- Output: per-route probability that a warm instance will be required in the next prediction window (score 0.0–1.0).

2) Policy engine and warm decisions
- Warm thresholds: configurable by tier and route. Default: score >= 0.7 triggers warmup request.
- Fiscal caps: per-tenant warm_budget_percent (default 5%), max_warm_instances (default 3 for small tenants).
- Priority classes: high (SLO-backed), medium (growth), low (best-effort). High-priority customers may have dedicated warm pool for SLA-backed routes.

3) Warm execution path
- Pre-warm flow: optimizer -> allocation API -> long-lived warm pod with preloaded model variant and quantization runtime -> health probe -> mark as warm.
- Warm retention: TTL-based with activity extension and an eviction score combining recency, prediction score, and cost sensitivity.

4) Cost accounting and telemetry
- Warm instances carry a meta-label (warmup=true) for billing and telemetry joins. Warm hours recorded and surfaced in Console under "Warmup economics".
- Telemetry: per-route warmup decisions, latency delta (cold vs warm), incremental GPU-hours, and warm-request hit rate.

Service and config table (example):
- service_owner: eng-platform@redwood.com
- api_surface: POST /v1/allocator/prewarm (internal)
- prediction_window_seconds: 60
- default_threshold: 0.7
- warm_instance_ttl_seconds: 300
- warm_budget_percent_default: 0.05
- max_warm_instances_default: 3

Requirements (MUST):
- MUST expose per-tenant toggles: enabled (bool), budget_percent (float), max_instances (int).
- MUST annotate allocation and billing events with warmup=true label.
- MUST provide Console charts for: warm hours, warm hit rate, cold tail latency trend, incremental spend estimate.
- MUST respect dedicated/dedicated-shared isolation: Private and Dedicated instances can opt into warmup only with customer consent.
- MUST support safe fallback: when predictor fails or is unhealthy, system reverts to conservative baseline of not pre-warming (configurable).

Requirements (SHOULD):
- SHOULD offer a "cost-prioritized" mode that lowers threshold adaptively when price per token drops below tenant's price floor.
- SHOULD surface candidate warmup explanations per decision for first 30s to aid debugging (why pre-warmed: spike in rate, recent session churn, etc.).

Non-goals:
- Not intended to replace long-term capacity planning or Reserved Dedicated contracts.
- Not a quality-safety heuristic for hallucination mitigation.

Telemetry, metrics and SLOs:
- Primary metrics:
  - warmup_decisions_per_minute (per-route)
  - warm_instance_uptime_seconds
  - warm_hit_rate = requests_served_by_warm / total_requests
  - latency_p99_cold (baseline)
  - latency_p99_with_warm
  - incremental_gpu_hours_from_warmup
- SLO targets for launch experiment cohort:
  - latency_p99_with_warm <= latency_p99_cold * 0.6 (i.e., 40% reduction) for 80% of targeted routes
  - warm_cost_percent <= tenant_budget_percent + 2% (variance allowance) for 80% of tenants in the cohort

Safety, privacy and compliance:
- Warmup telemetry contains only resource labels and aggregate counts. No customer prompt payloads are used by predictor.
- Private deployments: warmup feature disabled by default; can be enabled by customer-managed config.
- Audit logs: every warm decision and allocation emits an audit event stored in audit-logging service with 90-day retention.

Operational playbook (runbook summary):
1) Trigger for investigation:
  - warm_cost_percent increases > 10% for > 1 hour for cohort customers
  - warm_hit_rate < 5% while warm hours > 1% of total
  - predictor service CPU spikes or error rate > 2%
2) Immediate mitigation steps:
  - Toggle per-tenant warmup.enabled=false via admin console OR reduce warm_budget_percent to 0.0
  - Roll predictor to previous stable model via optimize-predictor rollback endpoint
  - Notify SRE pager if allocation errors > 1%
3) Recovery and follow-up:
  - Re-run offline simulation using recorded telemetry, tune threshold and TTL, and run small A/B test
  - Prepare RCA if incident impacted SLOs or cost budgets (owner: Eng Platform)

Data model and storage:
- Predictor stores short-term sliding window features in tsdb (servicename: warm-predictor-tsdb) with TTL 7 days.
- Decisions persisted in decisions-store for 30 days for audit and offline training.

Rollout plan and experiments:
Phase 0 — Lab (Q2 2027, internal):
- Implement predictor prototype and dry-run (no allocations). Validate signal quality on 50 synthetic routes.
- Success criteria: predictor precision >= 0.6 at threshold 0.7 and no runaway allocations in simulator.

Phase 1 — Canary (Q3 2027):
- Target 5% of hosted customers (opt-in) across small/medium/large segmentation. Enable warmup with conservative defaults (budget 3%).
- Monitor warm_cost_percent, warm_hit_rate, latency_p99_cold vs with_warm.
- Rollback if incremental cost > 7% for > 24h in canary cohort.

Phase 2 — Controlled ramp (Q4 2027):
- Expand to 25% customers. Introduce cost-prioritized mode for price-sensitive tenants. Add console billing visibility and alerting.

Phase 3 — Global availability (Q1 2028):
- Feature GA. Offer dedicated warm-pool SKUs for SLA-backed customers and pricing add-on.

Pricing and packaging notes:
- Beta pricing (canary): warm hours are tracked but not billed (cost shown for transparency).
- GA pricing options:
  - Consumption mode: customers pay per warm_hour at a discounted rate relative to on-demand GPU-hour (example: 0.45x on-demand)
  - Bundle mode: enterprise add-on where warm pool capacity is reserved as part of Dedicated contracts with guaranteed warm capacity and predictable monthly fee.
- Pricing guardrails: warm-budget-percent exposed in Console influences billing alert thresholds. Default alerts at 5% above budget.

Console UX and customer controls:
- Toggle (per-tenant): Enabled / Disabled / Opt-in (preview)
- Budget slider: 0%–20% with warnings beyond 10%
- Quick diagnostics: recent warm decisions, latency impact, top affected routes, and cost estimate per day

APIs and CLI examples (internal):
- Example allocation call (internal):
  curl -X POST https://allocator.internal.redwood/api/v1/prewarm \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \n    -d '{"tenant_id":"t-123","model_variant":"gptx-14b-q4","priority":"high","ttl":300}'

- Toggle via admin API:
  PATCH /api/v1/tenants/t-123/config 
  payload: {"features":{"predictive_warmup": {"enabled": true, "budget_percent": 0.03}}}

Risk analysis and mitigations:
- Risk: Overfitting predictor to noisy short-term signals -> mitigation: bayesian prior and cooldown windows, offline backtesting required before rollouts.
- Risk: Unexpected cost spikes -> mitigation: hard budget caps, automatic rollback triggers, billing alerts.
- Risk: Interference with Dedicated isolation -> mitigation: explicit opt-in and contractual add-on for dedicated SKUs.

Ownership and success criteria:
- Product owner: Priya Nambiar (product)
- Engineering owners: Eng Platform (owner alias: eng-platform), Optimize Conductor (optimize-team@redwood.com)
- SRE contact: Marcus Li (eng-sre)
- Launch success criteria (to GA):
  - 99th-percentile cold-start latency reduced by >=40% for 80% of canary routes
  - Incremental warmup spend within budget for 85% of canary tenants
  - Console telemetry and rollback controls implemented and validated

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Which model architectures (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, multimodal) show different warm initialization costs and how should thresholds differ?
- Should warmup decisions include kernel/JIT warm-only vs full model load differentiation?
- Commercial: what is an acceptable price multiplier for warm_hour in large enterprise negotiations?

Appendix A — Simulation checklist for SRE/Product:
1) Recreate request traces for 72h and inject into simulator with realistic eviction events.
2) Run predictor in dry-run and record decision rate and false positives.
3) Simulate budget enforcement and ensure no tenant exceeds budget in >1h window.
4) Validate audit trail and Console reporting.

Appendix B — Example console wireframe notes:
- Dashboard panels: Warmup trend (7d), Warm cost by tenant (heatmap), Top warm-decisions (table), Route-level latency delta (sparkline).
